authors: Abu Jafar Saifullah, Tasmia Zerin, Zerina Begum, Kazi Sakib
title: NavA11y: A Dynamic Analysis Approach for WCAG 2.4 Focus-Behavior Evaluation
venue: In Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Evaluation of Novel Approaches to Software Engineering (ENASE 2026), Vol. 2, pp. 1019–1030. SCITEPRESS. Benidorm, Spain
status: Full paper · Presented in person, May 2026
method: Drives a real browser through each page's keyboard tab order and, at every focus stop, checks that focus lands where expected, is visibly indicated, and is not hidden behind other content.
keyResults: 100% precision and recall on a 22-page labeled dataset (32 SC-level assertions)
2,947 violations detected across 26 production websites; 90% precision validated by two independent expert raters
First tool to cover all five WCAG 2.4 focus-behavior success criteria

authors: Syed Fatiul Huq, Md. Asif Haider, Abu Jafar Saifullah, Thomas Zimmermann, Sam Malek
title: Vibing Accessibly: Investigating the Accessibility of Websites Generated by LLM Coding Agents
method: Generated 90 websites with three coding agents and four language models, audited complete user journeys with three accessibility checkers, re-ran 24 configurations with agent accessibility Skills, and ran user testing with blind participants.
keyResults: None of the 90 websites was fully accessible (80 violating elements on average, 13 WCAG criteria violated)
Skills significantly improved accessibility scores but did not remove all violations and lowered functional correctness
